points.description: States what the table holds: a mapping of stations/destination (MAC) addresses to outgoing LAN interfaces/ports.
points.partial_credit: Half if only vaguely says it holds addresses or ports without the mapping.

points.description: Describes how the table is modified during backward learning: starts empty; when a frame arrives with source address Q on LAN L, the bridge adds/updates an entry 'Q reachable via L' (timestamp used to refresh/purge old entries).
points.partial_credit: Half if it only says the bridge learns from the source address of incoming frames without the entry/update detail.

points.description: States how the table is used in forwarding (look up destination to forward selectively on the right link instead of flooding) and gives one benefit (e.g. less unnecessary traffic/congestion, better bandwidth use).
points.partial_credit: Half if only use or only benefit is given.

rubric.notes: Full marks for covering all parts in any wording: table contents, learning from source addresses of incoming frames, and selective forwarding with one benefit. Give part marks for right-track but vague or incomplete parts. Give nothing for parts that are missing or wrong; extra incorrect remarks do not cost marks unless they contradict the main idea.
